change: Clarify dropped-gun recovery and owned weapons in play, revise relay geometry, and rebalance movement audio

baseline.pickup: A dropped gun was visible only nearby, with an interaction sentence at 60 world units; touch showed the keyboard E prompt and the HUD showed only the next owned gun.
baseline.relay: The world objective was two plain boxes with one emissive top plate.
baseline.audio: The footfall had a strong high-frequency strike and a single 60 ms gate shared by every actor.

observed.recovery: Native rules retain the previous gun on new-gun pickup and transfer same-type drop rounds to capped reserve; the match HUD now identifies those outcomes and shows a visible drop before interaction range.
observed.weapons: Deathmatch exposes three immediate alternative weapon buttons on desktop, a next-gun button on touch, and the full 12-gun armory. Demolition begins with one gun until purchases or recovery.
observed.relay: The original R-7 relay mesh has a power core, status face and antenna silhouette; cyan channels change to amber when planted. A visible device added 22 draw calls in the sampled SwiftShader scene (48 hidden, 70 visible).
observed.footsteps: Local and remote steps have separate cadence limits; remote steps play at half the local step level at equal spatial level. The new samples are 110, 125 and 190 ms for the two steps and landing.

checks.native: cargo test --manifest-path botstrike/Cargo.toml: 33/33 passed, including dropped-gun, same-type ammo, capacity, line of sight and objective-priority cases.
checks.pickupBrowser: Native practice plus synthetic visible-drop snapshots: keyboard and touch interaction packets, recovery wording, marker approach, drop removal and six required viewports passed.
checks.armoryBrowser: Native practice: rejected unowned choice, direct desktop equip, touch next-gun equip and armory equip passed.
checks.audioBrowser: Native practice started revised running and landing buffers alongside weapon and impact samples without page errors.
checks.relayBrowser: Visible versus hidden draw calls, planted capture and frame-pixel variation passed at 1920x1080, 2560x1080, 2560x1440, 3840x2160, 390x844 and 844x390, plus a touch-enabled 844x390 capture.
checks.hardware: Apple M4 Max; Playwright Chromium headless shell 1234 using SwiftShader software rendering.

limits: The browser drop snapshots are synthetic UI fixtures; native pickup behavior is covered by Rust tests, not a human encounter in this run.
No human listening comparison, physical speakers or headphones, real mobile GPU frame pacing, or human multiplayer playtest was performed.
The local improvements branch has not been pushed, opened as a PR or deployed; the public store may still show the older build.
